newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico tribe reopens casino.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico tribe reopens casino.

text.p: A New Mexico Indian tribe reopened its casino on Friday after striking a temporary deal with federal government officials.

The Mescalero Apaches reopened the doors of their "Casino Apache" in southern New Mexico in time for business Friday night, and will be allowed to continue until a long-running legal battle over Indian gaming in New Mexico is resolved in the courts.

The Mescalero were forced to close their casino in late September after a federal judge turned down their appeal against a court ruling that all the state's casinos were illegal. Ten other New Mexico gaming tribes fought successful legal actions to keep their casinos open, pending a final decision on the dispute.

"There is no reason in principle to treat the Mescalero Apache any differently from other gaming tribes in New Mexico," said U.S. Attorney John Kelly, who had enforced the initial shutdown of the Mescaleros' casino.

In cutting the deal with Kelly, Mescalero leaders agreed to close down their casino for good if an appeal lodged with the 10th Circuit District Court by the state's gaming tribes is unsuccessful. The court is considering the appeal but no date has been set for a ruling.
